Predicates:
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is provided financial aid.
ProveHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
LivesInFamily(x, y) ::: x lives in family y.
HasResources(x) ::: x has resources available.
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to y.
GRETest(y) ::: y is a GRE test.
Cost(y, z) ::: the cost of y is z.
CheaperThan(y, z) ::: y costs less than z.
Employer(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
FamilyFamily(x, y) ::: x and y are family members.
Year(y) ::: y is a year.
Published(y, z) ::: y is published in year z.
Author(x, y) ::: x is the author of y.
Book(x) ::: x is a book.
Specialize(x, y) ::: x specializes in y.
Love(x, y) ::: x loves y.
MiroslavVenhoda ::: Miroslav Venhoda.
Czech(x) ::: x is a Czech person.
ChoralConductor(x) ::: x is a choral conductor.
Musician(x) ::: x is a musician.
Music ::: music (as a constant).
Research(x, y) ::: x researches y.
Renaissance ::: Renaissance music.
Baroque ::: Baroque music.
MethodOfStudyingGregorianChant ::: the book.
Year1946 ::: the year 1946.
CostOfGRE ::: the cost of GRE test.
CheaperThanGRE ::: GRE cost is less than 300.
ApplyingToGRE(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE.
Family(x) ::: x is a family.
Resources(x) ::: x resources.
FamilyMember(x, y) ::: x is a family member of y.
Premises:
Cost(CostOfGRE, 205) ∧ CheaperThanGRE(CostOfGRE, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (ProveHardship(x) → (SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x))) ::: Those proving hardship can be from a single-parent family or have few resources.
LivesInFamily(Tom, family) ∧ FamilyMember(family, Tom) ::: Tom lives in a family.
SingleParentFamily(Tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
Resources(Tom) ∧ FewResources(Tom) ::: Tom has few resources available.
Applying(Tom, GRETest) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
¬∃x (Applying(x, GRETest) ∧ FinancialAid(x)) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
